title: Historical memory prices 1960-2026
summary: Stanford University's Digital Asset Manager hosts a comprehensive dataset tracking memory (RAM) prices from 1960 to 2026, illustrating the dramatic exponential decline in memory costs over six decades. This data demonstrates the Moore's Law-like trend where memory has become increasingly affordable, with prices per unit dropping by orders of magnitude.
problem_solved: Provides historical pricing data showing how memory costs have decreased exponentially over 60+ years
why_valuable: Offers empirical evidence of technological progress and cost reduction in computing hardware, useful for research and understanding industry trends
